name: MonarchAiPermissionScope
title: AiPermissionScope
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of FlowRow rows; androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton for the editable control; MonarchFavicon, MonarchLink
summary: What an AI agent may read or edit, app by app: each row names the app and the resources it covers and shows No access, Can read or Can read and edit, or a None / Read / Write control when editable.
whenToUse: In assistant settings or before connecting an agent, to show or change what it may see and change in each connected app.
whenNotToUse: For a single yes/no permission use MonarchSwitchRow. For the system permissions of the device (microphone, location) use the Android permission request.
api: @Composable fun MonarchAiPermissionScope(scopes: List<MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, onScopesChange: ((List<MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem>) -> Unit)? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, accessIcon: (@Composable (MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels = MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(), onManage: (() -> Unit)? = null)
data class MonarchAiPermissionScopeItem(app: String, access: MonarchAiAccessLevel, resources: String? = null, icon: Painter? = null)
enum class MonarchAiAccessLevel { None, Read, Write; fun includes(needed: MonarchAiAccessLevel): Boolean }

class MonarchAiPermissionScopeLabels(label: String? = null, access: ((MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = null, option: ((MonarchAiAccessLevel) -> String)? = null, control: ((app: String) -> String)? = null, manage: String? = null, empty: String? = null)

options.name: scopes
options.description: One row per app, each with a unique app name, the access level, optional resources and an optional icon Painter.

options.name: onScopesChange
options.description: Makes the list editable: called with the whole list, one row changed, when the person picks another level. Pass the new list back in scopes. null shows the access as text.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the editable controls take input.

options.name: accessIcon
options.description: An icon before the access text of a read-only row, given the level (for example a lock, an eye or a pencil). Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the list name, the level texts, the short option names, the control name, the manage text and the empty text.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds a "Manage permissions" link under the list.

states.name: read only
states.description: Each row writes the level: No access in muted text, Can read, Can read and edit, with the optional access icon.

states.name: editable
states.description: Each row has a None / Read / Write segmented control; the chosen segment is filled and has a check mark.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When the access or the control does not fit beside the app name, it moves under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: "The AI has no access to any app." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled false the segments use the disabled roles and take no input.

appearance: App names are strong body text with resources in muted caption text; rows are separated by the subtle border color. The segmented control is the Material 3 one in the Monarch theme. The manage link is the standalone MonarchLink in the link color. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's manageHref link becomes an onManage callback, as on iOS, since a native app opens its own settings screen. The web's onChange(scopes, changed) and iOS's binding become onScopesChange with the whole list. The app icon is a Painter shown with MonarchFavicon (iOS takes a URL; Monarch for Android loads no images). The web draws lock, eye and pencil glyphs; Android bundles no icons, so they are the accessIcon slot and the level is always written. The parity map named a LazyColumn; the list is a Column, because a permission list is short and usually sits in a settings screen that already scrolls, where a nested LazyColumn cannot be measured.
accessibility: The list is a TalkBack traversal group named "What the AI can access".
A read-only row is one element read as the app and its resources, with the access ("Can read") as its state description.
The level is always written, so it never depends on color or on an icon.
An editable row's control is a traversal group named "Access to <app>"; each segment keeps the Material 3 radio button role and selected state.
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
Segments and the manage link have touch targets of at least 48dp by 48dp; rows wrap and stack at large font sizes.
edgeCases: App names must be unique: they are the rows' identity.
An empty or blank resources string is not shown or read.
Picking the level a row already has does not call onScopesChange.
Long app names and resources wrap; the control moves under them.

examples.title: Read-only
Editable, with a manage link
examples.code:
MonarchAiPermissionScope(
    scopes = scopes,
    onScopesChange = { scopes = it },
    onManage = {},
)
